questions.question: Why do long agent tasks fail even with a capable model?
options: One context window can't hold the whole history, and one process may not survive until the end
Tools stop working after an hour
questions.explanation: Context limits and process lifetime are separate problems with a shared fix: state on disk.

questions.question: Why does the todo file use write-temp-then-rename?
options: The rename is atomic, so a crash never leaves a half-written todo file
questions.explanation: Readers see either the old file or the new one, never a corrupt mix.

questions.question: A new session finds an item marked in_progress. What should it do first?
options: Run its check: the previous session may have finished the edit or stopped halfway
questions.explanation: In-progress means unverified. Check, then fix or mark done.

questions.question: Who decides when a session hands off?
options: The model, when it notices its context is full
The harness, when the transcript passes the budget; the model then writes the note
questions.explanation: The model can't see its own context size. The harness measures and tells it when.

questions.question: Peak context per session stayed around 6,600 characters. What happens to a single unbounded session as the task grows?
options: It keeps growing with every item (12,671 chars for 8 modules here), until quality drops or the window overflows
questions.explanation: Bounded sessions keep cost and quality flat no matter how long the task is.

questions.question: How does a handoff differ from in-place compaction?
options: Compaction summarises the transcript to keep one session going; a handoff ends the session and restarts from files, which also survives crashes
questions.explanation: Files are the source of truth for handoffs, not a summary of a transcript.
